questions.question: What is most important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing when buying a helmet. Choose a helmet that fits well, fastens securely, and meets DOT safety standards.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake and rear brake at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front brake and rear brake at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time with controlled pressure. Be careful not to lock the brakes.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while stopping, release the front brake immediately and then press it firmly again. Use both brakes together when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Using both brakes together helps you stop quickly and safely.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Position the motorcycle so other drivers can see it.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Prepare the clutch and brakes to react quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, slow down. Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. Do not change speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is most easily seen by other drivers when riding in which lane position?
questions.explanation: When traffic allows, ride in the center lane position. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror where they can see you. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or road conditions require it.

questions.question: _________ of motorcycle-vehicle collisions happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle-vehicle collisions happen because drivers do not yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume that drivers of larger vehicles will yield to you, even if the law requires them to.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use the front and rear brakes together and downshift gears.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, how should you position yourself?

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle. Your arms should not be used to hold up your body or support your weight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers what traffic laws apply. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Ride within the posted speed limits.
Exceed the posted speed limit to complete the pass, but not by more than 10 mph.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride within the posted speed limits.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the speed limit. Pass only where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: What can best help protect you from serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best defense. A plastic face shield protects your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do first?

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as they are on your motorcycle.
Immediately take it out on the highway.
Get familiar with it in a controlled area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get familiar with it in a controlled area.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Learn where all the controls are before riding. Practice in a controlled area before going on the road.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely enough to allow the wind to catch the fabric.
Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
Be tight enough to prevent you from moving freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind. They should still be loose enough for you to move freely.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: The front tire affects your steering, which also affects your balance.
The front tire being flat will disable the front brake.
The front tire being flat will prevent you from accelerating.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire affects your steering, which also affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes it hard to steer. Good steering is essential for balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Tell other drivers that you are riding near them.
Help other drivers see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
Warn other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light to warn other drivers when you are slowing down or stopping in places where they don't expect it. This is especially important before making a tight, fast turn off a high-speed road.

questions.question: To be more visible, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in bad weather.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. This is the best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do these actions separately. Do not brake while swerving because this can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.
questions.explanation: Poor traction can happen on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement, gravel roads, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Drift into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to drift into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.
